findings.subject: entity-anti-nephrin
findings.text: A pediatric and young-adult idiopathic nephrotic syndrome cohort detected anti-nephrin antibodies in 15% of MCD and 11% of FSGS patients. This qualifies the higher adult MCD prevalence reported in another cohort: positivity is assay-, population- and activity-dependent and is not specific to MCD.
findings.quote: with a higher prevalence among those with nephrotic-range proteinuria.
findings.studySystem: Human pediatric and young-adult biopsy-proven MCD/FSGS; ELISA with immunoprecipitation confirmation.
limitations: Cross-cohort prevalence comparisons are not controlled head-to-head assay comparisons.
Association with activity and glycosylation does not establish causal sufficiency.
findings.distinctFindingRationale: Separate cohort added following actual external summary feedback; not independent replication of multiple readouts from the same paper.

findings.subject: entity-anti-nephrin
findings.text: A cell-based assay study detected anti-nephrin antibodies in 7/36 adults with MCD (19.44%) and 7/26 with nephrotic proteinuria (26.92%). This qualifies higher prevalence from other assays/cohorts; a negative test does not exclude MCD.
findings.quote: The prevalence of circulating anti-nephrin antibody was 19.44% (7 of 36) in MCD
findings.studySystem: Human adult cohort: 36 MCD among 108 glomerular disease patients plus 20 healthy controls; cell-based indirect immunofluorescence.
limitations: Small selected cohort and assay-specific diagnostic estimates; not population prevalence.
The study does not identify why prevalence differs across cohorts.
findings.distinctFindingRationale: Separate cohort added following actual external summary feedback; not independent replication of multiple readouts from the same paper.
